name: Hiller UH-12 / OH-23 Raven
summary: Mid-century three-seat piston light helicopter famous for its control paddles; widely flown for ag spraying, training and as the military OH-23 Raven.

wings: Two-blade main rotor with a pair of small servo paddles on short bars at the hub, set 90 degrees to the blades
No stabilizer bar above the rotor head
engines: Piston engine behind the cabin (turbine on Soloy conversions)
Agricultural machines usually carry a hopper and spray booms
fuselage: Rounded goldfish-bowl bubble canopy over a three-seat bench
Skids; spray booms or float kits are common
tail: Slim tail boom ending in a two-blade tail rotor
Small ventral fin under the boom protects the tail rotor

tellTales: Small paddles on short bars at the hub, turned 90 degrees to the two blades
Goldfish-bowl bubble canopy with a three-seat bench
Often seen with spray booms and a hopper

confusedWith.howToTell: The Bell 47 has a stabilizer bar with paddle tips above the rotor head and a distinctive open boom; the Hiller has small paddles on short bars at the hub and no bar above.
The Alouette has three main blades, a turbine perched on top and an open lattice boom; the Hiller has two blades with paddles and a piston engine.
The R44 has no paddles on its thin two-blade rotor and has two seat rows; the Hiller has the hub paddles and a single bench seat.
